claim: 4Q26 forecast: NAND Flash contract prices up 15% to 20% quarter on quarter, enterprise SSD up 23% to 28%
source: TrendForce, 4Q26 Memory Price Forecast, public summary (2026-09-24)
note: A forecast, not a realised price; the sixth consecutive quarter of increases in the cycle.

claim: AI server orders of $60.9 billion in the quarter to July 31, 2026 against $16.4 billion shipped; AI server backlog of $95 billion, about 5.8 quarters of shipments at the current rate
source: Dell Technologies Q2 FY2027 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-09-01)
note: Orders outrunning what can be built and shipped; the same release raised the fiscal-2027 AI server outlook to $74 billion.

claim: US primary colocation markets at mid-2026: a record 7,481 MW under construction, 80.4% of it preleased, and a record-low vacancy of 1.4%
source: CBRE, North America Data Center Trends H1 2026 (2026-08-27)
note: Built supply is spoken for before it is delivered; almost none of the pipeline relieves vacancy.

claim: DRAM and NAND expected to absorb 47% of major cloud providers' capital expenditure in 2026 and 68% in 2027 at current prices
source: TrendForce press release (2026-08-25)
note: Memory is taking share of the same capex dollar that buys GPUs and buildings; a bottleneck that reprices the whole server.

claim: More than $25 billion of net new customer commitments added in early Q3 2026, on top of the $104 billion backlog at June 30
source: CoreWeave Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-08-11)
note: Roughly two quarters of contracts signed at the model's assumed pace, in one announcement.

claim: Active power reached 1.5 GW and total contracted power about 3.7 GW at June 30, 2026; nearly 500 MW went live in the quarter
source: CoreWeave Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-08-11)
note: Already in data/disclosed/CRWV.csv; here as the latest capacity signal.

claim: Fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of $8.97 billion, up 51% quarter on quarter, about one-third from volume and two-thirds from price; fiscal 2026 revenue $20.25 billion, up 175%
source: Sandisk fiscal Q4 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-08-05)
note: The price signal arriving in the income statement eighteen months after the first customer letter.

claim: Signed load agreements of 69 GW for load coming online by 2030 across its PJM, SPP and ERCOT utilities, 6 GW added in the quarter; the same figure was 24 GW a year earlier
source: American Electric Power Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-07-30)
note: Contracted load at one utility, not requests; a floor on the demand the grid stage must connect.

claim: 2026 capital expenditure guided to the high KRW 40 trillion range, against KRW 27.5 trillion in 2025
source: SK hynix Q2 2026 earnings call, transcript (2026-07-28)
note: Supply response to the price cycle; new DRAM fabs take two to three years, so the response lands in 2028.

claim: Gas turbine equipment backlog of 53 GW plus 63 GW of slot reservations, 116 GW in all, against output of about 20 GW a year; at least 125 GW under contract expected by the end of 2026
source: GE Vernova Q2 2026 results (Form 8-K, 2026-07-22)
note: About six years of current output: a turbine ordered now is delivered around 2030, which sets the lead time of firm power.

claim: 3Q26 forecast: conventional DRAM contract prices up 13% to 18% quarter on quarter, NAND Flash up 10% to 15%
source: TrendForce press release (2026-07-03)
note: Gains moderating from the 93% to 98% of 1Q26 but still rising.

claim: Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93% to 98% quarter on quarter in 1Q26 and the DRAM industry's revenue rose 81%
source: TrendForce press release (2026-06-01)
note: The loudest price signal in the chain; the 2025 NAND move led by Sandisk is the precedent.

claim: Chief executive: surpassed 1 GW of active power and on the way to more than 8 GW by 2030
source: CoreWeave Q1 2026 earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1, 2026-05-07)
note: From 1.5 GW at June 2026 this needs about 360 MW a quarter through 2030; the register assumes 350.

claim: Large-load interconnection requests of 75 MW and above reached 410 GW at March 26, 2026, about 87% of them data centres, up from 233 GW in December 2025
source: ERCOT update to the Texas House Committee on State Affairs (2026-04-09)
note: Requests, not firm demand: ERCOT's whole system peaks near 85 GW, so most of this will not be built.

claim: DDTL 4.0 facility with $8.5 billion of borrowing capacity at SOFR plus 2.25%, non-recourse to the parent, entered March 2026
source: CoreWeave 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (note 10)
note: Cheapest facility in the stack (7% effective); month disclosed, day not. The March 2026 filing is the source date.

claim: Sandisk shares closed 2025 at $237.38, 5.0 times the $47.15 close of February 18, 2025, its first week as a listed company, as NAND prices turned up
source: Yahoo Finance, SNDK historical prices
note: The market's read on the bottleneck: the 2025 case that set the standard for spotting one. Closed at $1,777.80 on 2026-09-25, 7.5 times the end-2025 price.

claim: The 2027/28 capacity auction cleared at the $333.44 per MW-day price cap with 134,479 MW procured, 6,623 MW short of the reliability requirement; PJM attributes nearly 5,100 MW of the higher requirement to data centres
source: PJM Inside Lines (2025-12-17)
note: A price cap that binds is a shortage measured in dollars; the cost lands on every PJM customer from June 2027.

claim: Price and volume agreements cover Micron's entire calendar 2026 HBM supply; fiscal 2026 capex plan raised to $20 billion
source: TrendForce News (2025-12-18) reporting Micron's fiscal Q1 2026 earnings call of 2025-12-17
note: Sold out a year ahead: HBM is allocated, not bought. Micron later raised fiscal 2026 capex to about $27 billion (June 2026 call).

claim: Five-year agreement to supply Microsoft with dedicated GPU capacity in tranches from a new data centre in Vineland, New Jersey; total contract value about $17.4 billion through 2031, with options that would increase it
source: Nebius Form 6-K, 2025-09-08
note: Cash flow from the agreement finances part of the associated capital expenditure. Subject to deployment and availability of the capacity.

claim: Second 2025 NAND price increase of 10% notified to customers, with the market expected to stay undersupplied through 2026
source: TrendForce News (2025-09-17), citing TechPowerUp's report of the customer letter
note: Second letter in six months; a further increase was reported in November 2025.

claim: Master services agreement under which OpenAI committed payments of up to approximately $11.9 billion
source: CoreWeave final prospectus (424B4, 2025-03-31), pp. 33 and 158
note: Disclosed in the final prospectus, not in the S-1 as first filed; the March 2025 backlog jump reflects it.

claim: Customer letter announcing NAND product price increases of more than 10% from April 1, 2025, citing tariffs, consumer inventory cuts and industry output cuts
source: Yahoo Finance / Investing.com (2025-03-07), reporting the customer letter
note: The first public sign of the 2025 NAND turn, three weeks after Sandisk's spin-off from Western Digital.
